newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn drops plan to expand Morsleben nuclear dump.
newsitem.headline: Bonn drops plan to expand Morsleben nuclear dump.

text.p: Germany's Environment Ministry said on Friday it had decided not to pursue a plan to expand an eastern German nuclear waste dump and said waste consignments would stop by the year 2003.

Bonn had been aiming to expand the Morsleben site but will now focus on two dumps in northern Germany, one at Gorleben for permanent storage of high-level waste and the other at Schacht Konrad for low and mid-level waste.

Popular opposition to the Gorleben dump and to nuclear waste shipments to it from processing plants have prompted massive demonstrations by environmentally-aware Germans who argue that the storage and transport of nuclear waste involve incalculable risks.
The Morsleben waste storage plant, started under the communist East German government, is Germany's only permanent dump but is suited only for low to mid-level nuclear waste.
The ministry said it would go ahead with plans to convert Gorleben and Schacht Konrad, both currently medium-term waste storage facilities, into permanent dumps.
The Morsleben site is not suitable for high-level nuclear waste and Germany has enough capacity at the other two sites, the ministry said.
